sources.title: Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch news release (29 October 2025): a leaked draft omnibus reform (the '11th Judicial Package') would amend the penal code so that acting 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' — or its promotion — carries up to three years in prison (an amendment to article 225 on 'indecent acts'), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under onerous eligibility rules, and allow criminal charges against trans people and the professionals who treat them; justified as protecting 'the family' and 'public morals'. HRW called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks of the decade and urged withdrawal.

Kaos GL (24 February 2026): presentation of its 'LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025', titled 'The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People'. Findings: anti-LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — targeting of LGBTI+ people as 'deviant' or 'a threat' by the president and senior officials raised officials' motivation and third-party impunity; the new Family Ministry became the implementing ministry; one LGBTI+ rights organisation was closed; platforms and broadcasters were penalised or withdrew; artistic events were cancelled. The report documents six violations of the right to life (three hate-motivated killings; trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (51 the previous year, largely during assemblies) and 313 liberty violations in 2025 (about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions). No official hate-crime statistics exist; cases rely on media.
